  ghidra/       Instruction export and translation tooling.
  verify_*.py   Behavioral comparison and independent assertion tools.
  build_*.ps1   Native build scripts; build_and_verify.ps1 assembles checks.
  analysis/     Instruction evidence, manifests and verification reports.
  project_status.json  Requirements, recovery details and scoped results.

The sibling ../../work/sonic-adventure directory contains local extracted
retail files, analysis workspaces and generated build products. Preserve
those locally for reproducibility. A source repository should distinguish
authored/recovered source from original disc assets and generated binaries.
No GitHub repository has been created or uploaded by this task.

Verification reports state their scope. A passing comparison with modeled
hardware or callbacks does not establish those modeled implementations.
Draft pseudocode and indexed functions are not finished decompilation.
Older aggregate counts in project_status.json are historical snapshots;
later named recovery/verification entries describe subsequent work.

Current filesystem milestone: native initialization and mount traverse the
original root directory (768 records) and SONICADV directory (2069 records).
BIOS, cache operations and some completion/device callbacks remain modeled.

Latest registered routine: sa_conditional_byte_clear_8c10e566 at 0x8c10e566.
Its 16-byte retail span is compared against the native implementation with
128 complete RAM and CPU-state cases, including both condition outcomes and
aliased byte destinations. Run build_and_verify.ps1 to repeat this check.

Latest registered overlay routine: sa_stg09_callback_0c9005ba at 0x0c9005ba.
Its 42-byte STG09.BIN span preserves the indirect/direct service sequence,
delay-slot arguments, saved/restored PR, and final tail target. It passes 128
comparisons over full 16 MiB RAM and CPU state, with service boundaries
captured. External service bodies and the final tail target remain outside its
scope. The build, verification, and registration are included in
build_and_verify.ps1.

Also recovered: sa_stg09_callback_0c9005e4 at 0x0c9005e4. Its 74-byte
state callback narrows the callback result, checks the signed counter byte,
restores the byte after its retail decrement/store/increment sequence, and
either returns or dispatches reason 45. It passes 192 full RAM, CPU and FPU
comparisons with service and dispatcher bodies intercepted at their call
boundaries. Run build_and_verify.ps1 to repeat this check.

Also recovered: sa_stg09_dispatch_helper_0c900c14 at 0x0c900c14. Its 30-byte
selector preserves the two recognized dispatches (12 and 34), their distinct
data-pointer registers, SR.T state, and the intentional self-loop for other
values. It passes 256 full 16 MiB RAM and CPU-state comparisons, with the
callee intercepted at its tail-call boundary. Run build_and_verify.ps1 to
repeat this check.

Also recovered: sa_stg09_task_callback_0c90116c at 0x0c90116c. Its 38-byte
callback saves the byte argument, calls the task allocator with the retail
arguments, then initializes the returned task's work-area word and byte. It
passes 96 full RAM and CPU-state comparisons, including three overlapping
stack/work-area cases. The allocator body is intercepted at its call boundary;
alias cases stop at the return-instruction boundary after comparing the return
address and all memory effects. Run build_and_verify.ps1 to repeat this check.

Also recovered: sa_stg09_task_callback_0c901192 at 0x0c901192. This sibling
task constructor initializes marker 0x1234 and stores its saved byte argument
in the returned task work area. It passes 96 full RAM and CPU-state comparisons,
including allocator-boundary and stack-alias cases. Run build_and_verify.ps1 to
repeat this check.

Also recovered: sa_stg09_leaf_0c901d20 at 0x0c901d20. Its six-byte body
subtracts 44 from SP and restores it in the RTS delay slot. The net effect is
a return through PR with all other CPU state and RAM unchanged; 64 complete
RAM/CPU comparisons pass. Run build_and_verify.ps1 to repeat this check.

Also recovered: sa_stg09_cleanup_callback_0c901d2a at 0x0c901d2a. This
100-byte task cleanup callback releases optional resources based on work-area
fields, calls a final cleanup service, restores PR/R14, and tail-transfers.
It passes 128 full RAM/CPU comparisons across every optional-service branch
combination. Service bodies are intercepted at their boundaries. Run
build_and_verify.ps1 to repeat this check.

Also recovered: sa_stg09_callback_setup_0c901c98 at 0x0c901c98. This
44-byte task initializer calls the retail setup service, sets the work-area
timer to 60, and installs both callback pointers. It passes 128 full RAM/CPU
comparisons with the service body intercepted at its boundary. Run
build_and_verify.ps1 to repeat this check.

Also recovered: sa_clear_0x600_bytes_8c107ec0 at 0x8c107ec0. Its fixed 0x600
byte clear, register outputs and status bit match retail in 64 full RAM and
CPU-state cases across mapped ranges. The cleared block's caller meaning is
still unidentified.

Also recovered: sa_zero_byte_range_check_8c11025c at 0x8c11025c. The native

Also recovered: sa_store_u16_be_8c111174 at 0x8c111174. It writes a 16-bit

Also recovered: sa_record_initialize_8c1082da at 0x8c1082da. Its ordered

Also recovered: sa_expand_bits_to_nibbles_8c108160 at 0x8c108160. It expands

Verifier-tooling finding (2026-10-13): `verify_startup.reference()` treats the supplied stop PC as a single global endpoint. When a hooked external service returns, the interpreter resumes at `state.pr`, so nested calls from a recovered routine cannot currently resume their internal continuation reliably. This blocks complete differential verification of some event-controller helpers such as STG09 `0x0c900040`. A partial, unregistered source experiment was removed. The verifier needs a resumable call-boundary/continuation API with explicit return-PC handling before those routines can be accepted; do not count that experiment as recovered code.
